description:
Runs Claude Code, Codex, Copilot CLI and other terminal coding agents together on one mission.

Runner is a native desktop application where terminal agents work together. Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Cursor CLI, Grok Build, Antigravity CLI, Copilot CLI and pi can take the same task in one mission, and each agent keeps its own TUI in a real terminal while the lead brings the decisions back to you. Everything in Runner is also a `runner` command: missions, crews, roles, projects, chats, sessions and messages are all addressable from the command line, with `runnerd` as the background service. Agents run natively on Windows without WSL, and PowerShell 7 is optional. Status: alpha, actively shipping. Native builds target macOS (Apple Silicon) and Windows (x64) on Windows 10 version 1809 or later; Intel Macs, Windows ARM64 and Linux are not supported. The installer, the application and the CLI sidecars are Authenticode-signed with a Certum open-source certificate issued to Open Source Developer Yicheng Wang.
Runner 0.19.8 is a feature release for macOS, Windows and Linux on top of 0.19.7, with agent version checks and background updates, new Usage settings and more reliable remote connections.
New
- Agent updates without blocking the window. Runner now refuses to start an agent version it knows is incompatible, starting with Codex below 0.149.0, instead of failing with confusing launch errors. Starting a chat, role or mission slot on an outdated agent updates it in the background: that pane waits until the update finishes while the rest of the window stays usable. Settings → Agents shows required and optional updates on each agent, a dot on the sidebar's Settings button points to them, and you can open the update's terminal if it asks for input. (#1165)
- Usage settings. Settings → Usage controls the sidebar usage badges, how often usage is checked, the five-hour limit window and near-limit notifications, with a compact preview of the sidebar footer. Checks stop when badges and alerts are both off. (#1249, #1271)
- Skills and MCP tabs for each agent. Each agent's Skills and MCP catalogs now live on that agent's own Settings page, next to a General tab. For Claude Code, they follow the selected account. (#1249)
- Launch options with a command preview. Settings → Agents adds a Launch card for each agent: Bypass for Codex and Claude Code chats (off by default), turning off Codex's remote plugin catalog, and turning off status hooks for chats. A copyable preview shows the exact chat and mission command Runner will run. (#1246)
- Switch sidebar views from the keyboard. ⌘. on macOS or Ctrl+. on Windows and Linux switches between the Projects and Active views and expands a collapsed sidebar. The shortcut can be rebound or removed in Settings and is in the command palette. On Windows and Linux, a terminal program that claims Ctrl+. still receives it first. (#1266)
Bug fixes
- More reliable remote connections. A remote window now notices a silently dropped network within about 15 seconds and reconnects, a single slow request no longer drops the whole connection, and typing survives short write stalls. On the host, one slow channel no longer holds up the others, and busy terminals no longer flood the relay. Reconnecting now shows as a centred pill over the terminal instead of a bar across it. (#1263)
- Restored Codex chats keep their colours. Restoring an archived Codex chat no longer paints the composer and your prompts in fallback colours. The chat restarts with a fresh terminal and keeps its conversation and launch settings. (#1257)
- Remote sidebars remember their view. A window connected to another computer remembers that host's sidebar filters and which projects and groups are collapsed. The first time you connect to a host, only projects with nothing open start collapsed. (#1272)
- Readable remote folder menu. The folder menu behind Change in a remote window's launcher is no longer squeezed to the width of the link. (#1238)
